objectives: Answer specific comprehension questions after listening to a short text [fk.k.hoer.1]
Read a short text and answer comprehension questions [fk.k.lesen.1]
Identify and produce passive voice sentences using be + past participle [fk.g.passive]
Open, continue, and close a conversation using at least 3 target phrases [fk.w.open_continue_close_conversations, fk.k.sprechen.1]

stages.name: Opening: Retrieval + Bridge + I can
stages.purpose: Activate prior knowledge of word order and past participle forms, then bridge to passive voice as today's target.

procedure.text: Quick fire (oral, whole class): give a subject-verb-object sentence about school; give past participles of clean, explain, give; give a greeting phrase; give a farewell phrase.
Think-write: write 2 active sentences about what happens in school.
Partner swap, compare sentences.
Bridge: 'You wrote sentences like The teacher explains the lesson. Today we flip it — the thing that receives the action comes first: The lesson is explained.'

Write I-can statements on board: I can answer questions about a text I hear. I can read a text and find passive sentences. I can change an active sentence to passive. I can open and close a conversation with 3 phrases.

stages.name: Listen + Comprehend
stages.purpose: Push listening from passive exposure to active comprehension by answering specific questions after two readings.

procedure.text: Pre-teach 3 words: caretaker (Hausmeister), form teacher (Klassenlehrer), timetable (Stundenplan). Students listen, books closed.
Read 'Back at School' aloud (first time). Students listen for gist: what is the text about?
Read 'Back at School' aloud (second time). Students answer the 3 listening MCQs while listening.
Students complete and submit listening MCQ answers.
Check answers together. Teacher highlights where each answer appears in the text.

stages.name: Read + Find Passives
stages.purpose: Deepen reading comprehension and make passive structures visible by combining targeted questions with passive-spotting.

procedure.text: Students open text and read independently. Answer the 3 reading comprehension MCQs.
Check reading MCQ answers together.
Mark the passive verb phrases: click every passive phrase in the 6 sentences exercise.
Check mark-the-words answers. Point out is/are + past participle pattern in each.

stages.name: Passive Production
stages.purpose: Move from recognition to production of passive forms using the grammar rule as a reference.

procedure.text: Show grammar explanation: passive = is/are + past participle. Run through the 3 before/after examples.
Gap-fill: complete 6 passive sentences using the hint word. Choose is or are yourself.
Reorder: unscramble 4 passive sentences from shuffled fragments. Stronger pupils add a by-phrase.
Check gap-fill and reorder answers together.

stages.name: Conversation Phrases + Speaking
stages.purpose: Pre-teach and produce functional phrases for opening, continuing, and closing a conversation.

procedure.text: Pre-teach 8 phrases in 3 groups using the glossary: 3 open, 3 continue, 2 close. Students copy into notebook.
Match each phrase to its function (open/continue/close) using the matching exercise.
Check matching answers.
Pairs practise a 6-line dialogue using one phrase from each group. Rotate partners once.
Two pairs perform their dialogue for the class.

stages.name: Wrap-up
stages.purpose: Formative check against I-can statements before dismissing.

procedure.text: Return to I-can statements — thumbs up/sideways/down per statement.
Note thumbs-down on passive production. Assign flashcards + homework for next lesson.

differentiationNotes: Weaker: formula card (is/are + past participle) visible throughout passive stages; scripted dialogue card for speaking. Stronger: no formula card for reorder, must add by-phrase; improvise dialogue beyond script.
exercisePlan: mcq — 3 listening comprehension questions on Back at School text [fk.k.hoer.1]
mcq — 3 reading comprehension questions on Back at School text [fk.k.lesen.1]
mark_the_words — click every passive verb phrase in 6 sentences [fk.g.passive]
gap_fill — complete 6 passive sentences with correct be + past participle form [fk.g.passive]
reorder — unscramble 4 passive sentences from shuffled fragments [fk.g.passive]
matching — match 8 conversation phrases to their function [fk.w.open_continue_close_conversations]
flashcards — 8 conversation phrase flashcards for self-study [fk.w.open_continue_close_conversations]
